A1.justification: Both PDFs describe PromptDresser and contain readable methods, equations, tables, figures, and supplementary material. Retained content can be matched across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark evaluations, text-alignment experiments, ablations, and a 40-participant user study, including supplementary results.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical evaluations and adds inference-time comparisons, annotation-agreement measurements, editability results, and further qualitative experiments.

M1.justification: Section 3 retains the SDXL architecture, separate person/clothing captions, random mask dilation, and coarse-to-fine prompt-aware mask generation. Grounded-SAM is named for the added outerwear demonstration, but no change to the algorithmic steps is specified.

E1.justification: VITON-HD, DressCode, and SHHQ-1.0 remain the benchmark coverage. v2 adds outerwear layering that preserves innerwear and demonstrations combining multiple garments (Figures 7 and 9), extending the tested scenarios without adding a named benchmark.

E2.justification: v2 removes HR-VITON and GP-VTON from Table 1 and removes HR-VITON from the corresponding qualitative comparisons. The five diffusion baselines, including OOTDiffusion despite its omission from the baseline-description paragraph, remain evaluated.

E3.justification: v2 substantially extends evaluation design through an approximately matched-latency comparison using 40-step IDM-VTON, a four-annotator study of 100 VITON-HD images using semantic textual similarity, and SSIM/LPIPS comparisons between tucked and untucked generations. The existing benchmark metrics, 2,032-image text-alignment evaluation, and 40-participant user study remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix D adds analyses of inference cost, LMM evaluator reliability, editability between prompt conditions, and performance with versus without mask augmentation under a coarse rectangular mask (Tables 7–9 and Figure 10). These substantially expand the existing holistic-caption, PMG, LLaVA, and stopping-parameter ablations.

E5.justification: Table 8 newly estimates annotation agreement using mean semantic textual similarity between GPT and human labels and between all human-annotator pairs. This adds a limited reliability statistic; repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, and formal significance tests remain unreported.

E6.justification: Tables 1, 2, and 4–6 revise numerous method and ablation scores. For example, VITON-HD SSIM/FID changes from 0.8530/8.64 to 0.8686/8.54, while DressCode upper-body SSIM changes from 0.9160 to 0.9308, overtaking IDM-VTON's retained 0.9267. Changes are not uniformly favorable: dresses FID changes from 11.04 to 11.09. Tables 7–9 add results, whereas Table 3 and the user-study percentages remain unchanged. The causes of the revised benchmark scores are not explained.

T1.justification: The diffusion objective, caption-generation formulation, and mask-dilation equation remain unchanged in Equations 1–3. Neither version provides additional theoretical results or proofs; the new evaluation metrics do not introduce formal theoretical developments.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same central claims: rich LMM-generated prompts improve controllable virtual try-on, adaptive masking preserves unrelated appearance, and the method achieves strong benchmark performance. The added applications support these claims without redefining them.

C2.justification: v2 adds interpretations concerning LMM–human agreement, PMG's computational overhead at comparable inference time, and applicability to layered outfits despite DressCode-only training. The existing limitations concerning SDXL's 77-token limit and manually constructed in-context examples remain.

D1.justification: v2 identifies Grounded-SAM for outerwear and reports inference times of 5.78 seconds/image for its models versus 5.84 for 40-step IDM-VTON. Existing SDXL, GPT-4o, Sapiens, 30-step inference, and mask-stopping settings move to Appendix C rather than being newly introduced. Prompt templates and the code link are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds IMAGDressing-v1 and explicitly distinguishes its inpainting prompting/masking approach from joint text-and-clothing conditioning. It also adds Grounded-SAM and two LMM-evaluation references while removing GP-VTON and several general diffusion references. The broader research positioning remains stable.

P1.justification: Substantial passages in the abstract, introduction, related work, and experimental discussion are rewritten or condensed. Baseline and implementation descriptions move from Section 4 to a new Appendix C, and the supplementary results are reorganized. The method exposition and prompt templates remain largely intact.

P2.justification: v2 redesigns Figure 1, removes the HR-VITON column and pose insets from Figure 4, rearranges qualitative comparisons, and exchanges some DressCode examples between the main text and appendix. It adds Figures 7, 9, and 10 and Tables 7–9. These are substantial display changes beyond numerical updates and renumbering.

improvement.justification: v2 adds useful direct evidence about mask augmentation, inference cost, and evaluator reliability that v1 lacked, particularly Figure 10 and Tables 7–8. These strengthen the paper's validation modestly. The gain is tempered by unexplained benchmark-score revisions, missing hardware and STS implementation details for the new checks, and removal of the GAN comparisons; higher reported scores alone do not establish improved quality.
